history.ask: Movement with swallowing or tongue protrusion (patient noticed)
options: Rises when sticking the tongue out
Palpitations, heat intolerance, weight loss with good appetite, tremor
Noisy breathing or breathlessness lying flat

history.ask: Fever, night sweats, or weight loss
Smoking, mouth ulcer, ear pain, or swallowing pain
Recent throat, dental, or scalp infection
Neck irradiation or family history of thyroid cancer

red_flags: Stridor or breathlessness lying flat — airway compression; urgent surgical referral
Rapidly growing hard fixed mass with hoarseness — anaplastic carcinoma or advanced malignancy; urgent surgical referral
Sudden painful thyroid enlargement — hemorrhage into a nodule threatening the airway
Lymph node with night sweats, fever, and weight loss — lymphoma or TB until proven
Hard lateral node in a smoker over 40 — metastasis from an occult head and neck primary until the primary is found
exam: Inspect from the front while the patient swallows water — a thyroid swelling rises with swallowing
Ask the patient to protrude the tongue — a midline lump that rises is a thyroglossal cyst
Palpate from behind: size, consistency (soft, firm, hard), single nodule vs multinodular, fixity to skin or deep structures
Try to get below the gland — inability plus dullness on sternal percussion means retrosternal extension
Perform Pemberton's maneuver — facial congestion on raising the arms indicates thoracic inlet obstruction
Palpate every cervical node station systematically on both sides — note matting (TB) vs rubbery (lymphoma) vs stony-hard (metastasis)
Assess thyroid status: pulse rate and rhythm, fine tremor, eye signs, skin
Auscultate over the gland for a bruit — supports a toxic goiter
Examine the mouth, tongue base, tonsils, and scalp for a primary lesion when a hard lateral node is found
Listen to the voice and document any hoarseness

investigations.why: First split in the pathway: a suppressed TSH points to a toxic nodule or toxic multinodular goiter — which is rarely malignant — while a euthyroid nodule proceeds to FNAC
Separates thyroid from non-thyroid lumps, grades nodules (solid, microcalcification, irregular margins favor carcinoma), shows a purely cystic thyroglossal or branchial cyst, and maps abnormal nodes

investigations.test: FNAC of the dominant nodule or node
investigations.why: The decisive clinic test: benign colloid vs papillary carcinoma in the thyroid; caseating granulomas rule in TB, and lymphoid or metastatic cells redirect to lymphoma or an occult primary
Very high ESR with cytopenias supports lymphoma or TB; leukocytosis supports an inflammatory/reactive node
Tracheal deviation or retrosternal shadow from a large goiter; mediastinal widening supports lymphoma; apical changes support TB
Second-line — if there is retrosternal extension, tracheal compression, or a fixed mass: defines the airway and extent before referral
